title: Tightness of the Gold-to-APN distance lower bound beyond dimension five
summary: Determine whether the source lower bound on the Hamming distance from the Gold function to another APN function is attained in any dimension greater than five.

formal_statement.body: For the Gold function $F(x)=x^3$ on $\mathbb F_{2^n}$, define the source Eq. (11) bound $B(n)$ by $B(n)=(2^{n-1}+2)/3$ when $n$ is odd, $B(n)=(2^{n-1}-2^{n/2-1}+2)/3$ when $n$ is even and $n/2$ is odd, and $B(n)=(2^{n-1}-2^{n/2}+2)/3$ when $n$ is even and $n/2$ is even. Determine whether there exist $n>5$ and an APN function $G\ne F$ such that $d(x^3,G)=B(n)$; equivalently, exhibit one attaining pair or prove strict inequality for every $n>5$.

scope.domain: Hamming distances between the Gold function and APN functions over binary finite fields
assumptions: $G:\mathbb F_{2^n}\to\mathbb F_{2^n}$ is APN and differs from $x^3$
$B(n)$ is the exact three-branch bound in source Eq. (11)
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later result constructs an attaining APN function for any n>5 or proves that the source Gold-function bound is always strict in this range. Later general distance bounds do not decide this equality question.

progress.summary: After proving and computing the Gold-function bound, the source asks whether it is attained in any dimension greater than five.
